sanskrit: evam uktvā tu paruṣaṃ mārīco rāvaṇaṃ tataḥ gacchāvety abravīd dīno bhayād rātriṃcaraprabhoḥ
english: Having spoken thus harshly, Mārīca then said to Rāvaṇa, "Let us go," reduced to submission by fear of the lord of night-wanderers.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaś cāhaṃ punas tena śaracāpāsidhāriṇā madvadhodyataśastreṇa vinaṣṭaṃ jīvitaṃ ca me
english: "I have again come face to face with him who bears bow, arrows, and sword, and whose weapon was raised for my slaying — my life is already as good as destroyed."

sanskrit: kiṃ tu kartuṃ mayā śakyam evaṃ tvayi durātmani eṣa gacchāmy ahaṃ tāta svasti te 'stu niśācara
english: "Yet what can I do when you, O wicked one, are like this? I shall go. May it be well with you, O night-wanderer."

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭas tv abhavat tena vacanena sa rākṣasaḥ pariṣvajya susaṃśliṣṭam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: That rākṣasa was overjoyed by those words; embracing him tightly, he spoke as follows.

sanskrit: etac chauṇḍīryayuktaṃ te macchandād iva bhāṣitam idānīm asi mārīcaḥ pūrvam anyo niśācaraḥ
english: "This speech of yours, full of courage, sounds as if it were said at my own bidding. Now you are truly Mārīca; formerly you were a different night-wanderer."

sanskrit: āruhyatām ayaṃ śīghraṃ khago ratnavibhūṣitaḥ mayā saha ratho yuktaḥ piśācavadanaiḥ kharaiḥ
english: "Mount quickly this sky-ranging chariot adorned with jewels, yoked with donkeys bearing the faces of piśācas, together with me."

sanskrit: tato rāvaṇamārīcau vimānam iva taṃ ratham āruhya yayatuḥ śīghraṃ tasmād āśramamaṇḍalāt
english: Thereupon Rāvaṇa and Mārīca mounted that chariot, which resembled an aerial vehicle, and departed swiftly from that hermitage-region.

sanskrit: tathaiva tatra paśyantau pattanāni vanāni ca girīṃś ca saritaḥ sarvā rāṣṭrāṇi nagarāṇi ca
english: As they traveled they observed towns and forests, mountains and all rivers, kingdoms and cities below.

sanskrit: sametya daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ rāghavasyāśramaṃ tataḥ dadarśa sahamarīco rāvaṇo rākṣasādhipaḥ
english: Arriving at the Daṇḍaka forest, the lord of rākṣasas, Rāvaṇa, together with Mārīca, then saw the hermitage of Rāghava.

sanskrit: avatīrya rathāt tasmāt tataḥ kāñcanabhūṣaṇāt haste gṛhītvā mārīcaṃ rāvaṇo vākyam abravīt
english: Descending from that golden-ornamented chariot and taking Mārīca by the hand, Rāvaṇa spoke these words.

sanskrit: etad rāmāśramapadaṃ dṛśyate kadalīvṛtam kriyatāṃ tat sakhe śīghraṃ yadarthaṃ vayam āgatāḥ
english: "That hermitage-site of Rāma, encircled by banana trees, is visible yonder. Friend, do swiftly that for the sake of which we have come."

sanskrit: sa rāvaṇavacaḥ śrutvā mārīco rākṣasas tadā mṛgo bhūtvāśramadvāri rāmasya vicacāra ha
english: Hearing those words of Rāvaṇa, the rākṣasa Mārīca thereupon transformed himself into a deer and began to roam about at the entrance of Rāma's hermitage.

sanskrit: maṇipravaraśṛṅgāgraḥ sitāsitamukhākṛtiḥ raktapadmotpalamukha indranīlotpalaśravāḥ
english: His horn-tips were of finest gems; his face was of mingled white and black hues, like a red lotus and a blue water-lily; his ears were like indranīla-blue lotuses.

sanskrit: kiṃ cid abhyunnata grīva indranīlanibhodaraḥ madhūkanibhapārśvaś ca kañjakiñjalkasaṃnibhaḥ
english: His neck was somewhat arched, his belly resembled the indranīla gem in hue, his flanks were like the madhūka flower, and his body was like the filaments of a lotus.

sanskrit: vaidūryasaṃkāśakhuras tanujaṅghaḥ susaṃhataḥ indrāyudhasavarṇena pucchenordhvaṃ virājitaḥ
english: His hooves resembled vaidūrya gems; his shanks were slender and well-knit; his tail, held aloft, gleamed with the colors of Indra's rainbow.

sanskrit: manoharasnigdhavarṇo ratnair nānāvidhair vṛtaḥ kṣaṇena rākṣaso jāto mṛgaḥ paramaśobhanaḥ
english: With a mind-entrancing, glossy complexion and covered all over with gems of many kinds, in an instant the rākṣasa became a deer of supreme beauty.

sanskrit: vanaṃ prajvalayan ramyaṃ rāmāśramapadaṃ ca tat manoharaṃ darśanīyaṃ rūpaṃ kṛtvā sa rākṣasaḥ
english: Illuminating the lovely forest and that hermitage-site of Rāma, the rākṣasa, having assumed that mind-enchanting, wondrous form—

sanskrit: pralobhanārthaṃ vaidehyā nānādhātuvicitritam vicaran gacchate samyak śādvalāni samantataḥ
english: —variegated with minerals of many kinds, for the purpose of enticing Vaidehī, moved about properly among the green meadows on all sides.

sanskrit: rūpyabinduśataiś citro bhūtvā ca priyadarśanaḥ viṭapīnāṃ kisalayān bhaṅktvādan vicacāra ha
english: Adorned with hundreds of silver spots and having become pleasing to behold, he wandered about, snapping off and nibbling the tender shoots of trees.

sanskrit: kadalīgṛhakaṃ gatvā karṇikārān itas tataḥ samāśrayan mandagatiḥ sītāsaṃdarśanaṃ tadā
english: Going toward the banana grove, resting now here now there among the karṇikāra trees, moving at a slow pace, he sought at that time to be seen by Sītā.

sanskrit: rājīvacitrapṛṣṭhaḥ sa virarāja mahāmṛgaḥ rāmāśramapadābhyāśe vicacāra yathāsukham
english: That great deer, his back dappled like a lotus, shone brilliantly as he wandered at ease in the vicinity of Rāma's hermitage.

sanskrit: punar gatvā nivṛttaś ca vicacāra mṛgottamaḥ gatvā muhūrtaṃ tvarayā punaḥ pratinivartate
english: That foremost of deer would go forward and then return, roaming about; having gone away for a moment with speed, he would come back again.

sanskrit: vikrīḍaṃś ca punar bhūmau punar eva niṣīdati āśramadvāram āgamya mṛgayūthāni gacchati
english: He would play again, then seat himself on the ground once more; approaching the hermitage gate, he would move off toward herds of deer.

sanskrit: mṛgayūthair anugataḥ punar eva nivartate sītādarśanam ākāṅkṣan rākṣaso mṛgatāṃ gataḥ
english: Followed by herds of deer, he would return once more — the rākṣasa, having assumed deer-form, yearning to be seen by Sītā.

sanskrit: paribhramati citrāṇi maṇḍalāni viniṣpatan samudvīkṣya ca sarve taṃ mṛgā ye 'nye vanecarāḥ
english: He wheeled about in varied circles, bounding through them; and all the other deer that roamed the forest looked up and saw him—

sanskrit: upagamya samāghrāya vidravanti diśo daśa rākṣasaḥ so 'pi tān vanyān mṛgān mṛgavadhe rataḥ
english: —approached him, sniffed him, and then fled in all ten directions. That rākṣasa, intent on the slaughter of deer, also pursued those wild deer—

sanskrit: pracchādanārthaṃ bhāvasya na bhakṣayati saṃspṛśan tasminn eva tataḥ kāle vaidehī śubhalocanā
english: —yet for the purpose of concealing his true nature he did not devour them even when he touched them. At that very time Vaidehī of lovely eyes—

sanskrit: kusumāpacaye vyagrā pādapān atyavartata karṇikārān aśokāṃś ca cūṭāṃś ca madirekṣaṇā
english: —intent on gathering flowers, was moving among the trees — karṇikāras, aśokas, and mango trees — she of intoxicating eyes.

sanskrit: kusumāny apacinvantī cacāra rucirānanā anarhāraṇyavāsasya sā taṃ ratnamayaṃ mṛgam muktāmaṇivicitrāṅgaṃ dadarśa paramāṅganā
english: Plucking flowers and roaming about with her lovely face — she who was undeserving of forest-life — that foremost of women beheld that gem-jeweled deer, its limbs variegated with pearls and precious stones.

sanskrit: taṃ vai ruciradaṃtauṣṭhaṃ rūpyadhātutanūruham vismayotphullanayanā sasnehaṃ samudaikṣata
english: That deer with beautiful teeth and lips, its body-hair like silver mineral, she gazed upon with eyes wide open in wonder, and with affection.

sanskrit: sa ca tāṃ rāmadayitāṃ paśyan māyāmayo mṛgaḥ vicacāra tatas tatra dīpayann iva tad vanam
english: And that deer, made of illusion, looking back at her — Rāma's beloved — roamed about there as if setting the forest ablaze with its brilliance.

sanskrit: adṛṣṭapūrvaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ nānāratnamayaṃ mṛgam vismayaṃ paramaṃ sītā jagāma janakātmajā
english: Never before having seen such a deer, all made of varied gems, Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, was seized by the greatest astonishment.

sanskrit: sā taṃ saṃprekṣya suśroṇī kusumāni vicinvatī hemarājatavarṇābhyāṃ pārśvābhyām upaśobhitam
english: She of beautiful hips, while gathering flowers, gazed intently at that deer adorned on both flanks with hues of gold and silver—

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭā cānavadyāṅgī mṛṣṭahāṭakavarṇinī bhartāram api cākrandal lakṣmaṇaṃ caiva sāyudham
english: —and, filled with delight, that woman of flawless limbs and the color of refined gold called out to her husband and also to Lakṣmaṇa bearing his weapons.

sanskrit: tayāhūtau naravyāghrau vaidehyā rāmalakṣmaṇau vīkṣamāṇau tu taṃ deśaṃ tadā dadṛśatur mṛgam
english: Those two tigers among men, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, called by Vaidehī, scanning that spot, then both saw the deer.

sanskrit: śaṅkamānas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇo rāmam abravīt tam evainam ahaṃ manye mārīcaṃ rākṣasaṃ mṛgam
english: But Lakṣmaṇa, suspicious upon seeing it, said to Rāma: "This deer — I take it to be none other than the rākṣasa Mārīca."

sanskrit: caranto mṛgayāṃ hṛṣṭāḥ pāpenopādhinā vane anena nihatā rāma rājānaḥ kāmarūpiṇā
english: "O Rāma, kings who roamed the forest on the hunt, rejoicing, have been slain in the forest by this wicked deceiver who changes form at will."

sanskrit: asya māyāvido māyāmṛgarūpam idaṃ kṛtam bhānumatpuruṣavyāghra gandharvapurasaṃnibham
english: "This form of an illusory deer has been fashioned by this master of māyā — O tiger among men of brilliant valor, it is like a city of the Gandharvas."

sanskrit: mṛgo hy evaṃvidho ratnavicitro nāsti rāghava jagatyāṃ jagatīnātha māyaiṣā hi na saṃśayaḥ
english: "For a deer of this kind, variegated with gems, does not exist anywhere in the world, O Rāghava, O lord of the earth — this is undoubtedly illusion."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ kākutsthaṃ prativārya śucismitā uvāca sītā saṃhṛṣṭā chadmanā hṛtacetanā
english: Interrupting Kākutstha who was speaking thus, Sītā of the pure smile spoke, thrilled with delight, her mind stolen away by the ruse.

sanskrit: āryaputrābhirāmo 'sau mṛgo harati me manaḥ ānayainaṃ mahābāho krīḍārthaṃ no bhaviṣyati
english: "O noble son, that deer ravishes my mind with its beauty. Bring it here, O mighty-armed one — it shall be our plaything."

sanskrit: ihāśramapade 'smākaṃ bahavaḥ puṇyadarśanāḥ mṛgāś caranti sahitāś camarāḥ sṛmarās tathā
english: "Here at our hermitage-site many auspicious-looking deer wander together — camaras, sṛmaras, and others—"

sanskrit: ṛkṣāḥ pṛṣatasaṃghāś ca vānarāḥ kiṃnarās tathā vicaranti mahābāho rūpaśreṣṭhā mahābalāḥ
english: "—bears, herds of spotted deer, monkeys, and kiṃnaras too roam here, O mighty-armed one, most beautiful in form and of great strength—"

sanskrit: na cāsya sadṛśo rājan dṛṣṭapūrvo mṛgaḥ purā tejasā kṣamayā dīptyā yathāyaṃ mṛgasattamaḥ
english: "—yet no deer equal to this one has ever been seen before, O king, in radiance, grace, and brilliance, as this foremost of deer."

sanskrit: nānāvarṇavicitrāṅgo ratnabindusamācitaḥ dyotayan vanam avyagraṃ śobhate śaśisaṃnibhaḥ
english: "With limbs variegated in many colors, studded all over with gem-spots, illuminating the forest serenely, it shines like the moon."

sanskrit: aho rūpam aho lakṣmīḥ svarasaṃpac ca śobhanā mṛgo 'dbhuto vicitro 'sau hṛdayaṃ haratīva me
english: "Ah, what beauty! Ah, what splendor! And what a lovely richness of voice! That wondrous, marvelous deer steals away my heart, it seems."

sanskrit: yadi grahaṇam abhyeti jīvann eva mṛgas tava āścaryabhūtaṃ bhavati vismayaṃ janayiṣyati
english: "If this deer comes to be captured alive by you, it would become a wonder and shall cause amazement."

sanskrit: samāptavanavāsānāṃ rājyasthānāṃ ca naḥ punaḥ antaḥpuravibhūṣārtho mṛga eṣa bhaviṣyati
english: "When our forest-exile is complete and we return to dwelling in the kingdom, this deer shall serve as an ornament for the inner apartments."

sanskrit: bharatasyāryaputrasya śvaśrūṇāṃ mama ca prabho mṛgarūpam idaṃ divyaṃ vismayaṃ janayiṣyati
english: "This divine deer-form shall cause amazement to noble Bharata, to my lord, to my mothers-in-law, and to myself, O lord."

sanskrit: jīvan na yadi te 'bhyeti grahaṇaṃ mṛgasattamaḥ ajinaṃ naraśārdūla ruciraṃ me bhaviṣyati
english: "If this foremost of deer does not come to be taken alive by you, O tiger among men, its beautiful hide shall be mine."

sanskrit: nihatasyāsya sattvasya jāmbūnadamayatvaci śaṣpabṛsyāṃ vinītāyām icchāmy aham upāsitum
english: "When this creature has been slain, I wish to sit upon its skin, which is made of jāmbūnada gold, spread out on a grass mat."

sanskrit: kāmavṛttam idaṃ raudraṃ strīṇām asadṛśaṃ matam vapuṣā tv asya sattvasya vismayo janito mama
english: "This excessive desire may be considered dreadful and unlike what is fitting for women — yet it is the wondrous beauty of this creature that has aroused it in me."

sanskrit: tena kāñcanaromṇā tu maṇipravaraśṛṅgiṇā taruṇādityavarṇena nakṣatrapathavarcasā babhūva rāghavasyāpi mano vismayam āgatam
english: By that deer with golden hair, with horns of finest gems, with the color of the newly risen sun, with the luminosity of the path of the stars — Rāghava's mind too was seized by wonder.

sanskrit: evaṃ sītāvacaḥ śrutvā dṛṣṭvā ca mṛgam adbhutam uvāca rāghavo hṛṣṭo bhrātaraṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having heard Sītā's words thus and having seen that wondrous deer, Rāghava, filled with delight, spoke to his brother Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehyāḥ spṛhāṃ mṛgagatām imām rūpaśreṣṭhatayā hy eṣa mṛgo 'dya na bhaviṣyati
english: "See, Lakṣmaṇa, this yearning of Vaidehī directed toward the deer. By reason of its supreme beauty this deer shall not escape today."

sanskrit: na vane nandanoddeśe na caitrarathasaṃśraye kutaḥ pṛthivyāṃ saumitre yo 'sya kaś cit samo mṛgaḥ
english: "Neither in Nandana forest nor in the domain of Caitraratha — where then in the whole earth, O son of Sumitrā, is there any deer equal to this one?"

sanskrit: pratilomānulomāś ca rucirā romarājayaḥ śobhante mṛgam āśritya citrāḥ kanakabindubhiḥ
english: "Lovely rows of hair, running both against and with the grain, adorned with golden spots of varied hues, shine beautifully upon this deer."

sanskrit: paśyāsya jṛmbhamāṇasya dīptām agniśikhopamām jihvāṃ mukhān niḥsarantīṃ meghād iva śatahradām
english: "See its tongue as it yawns — blazing, like a flame of fire, issuing from its mouth like lightning from a cloud."

sanskrit: masāragalvarkamukhaḥ śaṅkhamuktānibhodaraḥ kasya nāmānirūpyo 'sau na mano lobhayen mṛgaḥ
english: "With a face of masāra and galvarka gems, a belly resembling conch-shells and pearls — whose mind, tell me, would that deer of indescribable form not entice?"

sanskrit: kasya rūpam idaṃ dṛṣṭvā jāmbūnadamayaprabham nānāratnamayaṃ divyaṃ na mano vismayaṃ vrajet
english: "Upon seeing this form with the radiance of jāmbūnada gold, divine and made of gems of many kinds, whose mind would not be overcome by wonder?"

sanskrit: māṃsahetor api mṛgān vihārārthaṃ ca dhanvinaḥ ghnanti lakṣmaṇa rājāno mṛgayāyāṃ mahāvane
english: "Kings who are bowmen slay deer in the great forest during the hunt, O Lakṣmaṇa, for the sake of both their flesh and sport."

sanskrit: dhanāni vyavasāyena vicīyante mahāvane dhātavo vividhāś cāpi maṇiratnasuvarṇinaḥ
english: "Wealth is also sought through enterprise in the great forest, as are various minerals, along with gems, precious stones, and gold."

sanskrit: tat sāram akhilaṃ nṝṇāṃ dhanaṃ nicayavardhanam manasā cintitaṃ sarvaṃ yathā śukrasya lakṣmaṇa
english: "All that which is the wealth-essence of men — wealth that increases accumulation — is found here in the forest, just as it was conceived in the mind of Śukra, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: arthī yenārthakṛtyena saṃvrajaty avicārayan tam artham arthaśāstrajñaḥ prāhur arthyāś ca lakṣmaṇa
english: "The purpose for which a man in need of wealth roams without hesitation — that very wealth the knowers of artha-śāstra and wealthy men praise, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: etasya mṛgaratnasya parārdhye kāñcanatvaci upavekṣyati vaidehī mayā saha sumadhyamā
english: "On the supremely precious golden hide of this jewel among deer, the slender-waisted Vaidehī will sit with me."

sanskrit: na kādalī na priyakī na praveṇī na cāvikī bhaved etasya sadṛśī sparśaneneti me matiḥ
english: "Neither the kādalī, nor the priyakī, nor a rug, nor wool would be comparable to this in softness of touch — such is my judgment."

sanskrit: eṣa caiva mṛgaḥ śrīmān yaś ca divyo nabhaścaraḥ ubhāv etau mṛgau divyau tārāmṛgamahīmṛgau
english: "This glorious deer here, and that divine one who roams the sky — both are divine deer: the deer of the stars and the deer of the earth."

sanskrit: yadi vāyaṃ tathā yan māṃ bhaved vadasi lakṣmaṇa māyaiṣā rākṣasasyeti kartavyo 'sya vadho mayā
english: "Even if this is as you say to me, Lakṣmaṇa — that it is the māyā of a rākṣasa — then slaying him is all the more necessary for me."

sanskrit: etena hi nṛśaṃsena mārīcenākṛtātmanā vane vicaratā pūrvaṃ hiṃsitā munipuṃgavāḥ
english: "For it was by this cruel, unrestrained Mārīca, roaming the forest previously, that foremost sages were harmed."

sanskrit: utthāya bahavo yena mṛgayāyāṃ janādhipāḥ nihatāḥ parameṣvāsās tasmād vadhyas tv ayaṃ mṛgaḥ
english: "By him many kings, supreme archers, were slain after setting out on the hunt — therefore this deer must be killed."

sanskrit: purastād iha vātāpiḥ paribhūya tapasvinaḥ udarastho dvijān hanti svagarbho 'śvatarīm iva
english: "In former times Vātāpi here, having subdued ascetics and entered their bellies, slew brāhmaṇas from within, as a foetus destroys a mule."

sanskrit: sa kadā cic cirāl loke āsasāda mahāmunim agastyaṃ tejasā yuktaṃ bhakṣyas tasya babhūva ha
english: "Once, after a long time, he encountered in the world the great sage Agastya, endowed with spiritual power, and became his food."

sanskrit: samutthāne ca tad rūpaṃ kartukāmaṃ samīkṣya tam utsmayitvā tu bhagavān vātāpim idam abravīt
english: "Seeing him about to rise up and resume that form, the blessed one smiled and spoke these words to Vātāpi."

sanskrit: tvayāvigaṇya vātāpe paribhūtāś ca tejasā jīvaloke dvijaśreṣṭhās tasmād asi jarāṃ gataḥ
english: "'O Vātāpi, you have disregarded and by your power oppressed the foremost of brāhmaṇas in the world of the living — therefore you are now reduced to old age.'"

sanskrit: evaṃ tan na bhaved rakṣo vātāpir iva lakṣmaṇa madvidhaṃ yo 'timanyeta dharmanityaṃ jitendriyam
english: "Therefore, O Lakṣmaṇa, that rākṣasa would not fare otherwise than Vātāpi did — whoever disrespects one like me, constantly devoted to dharma and with conquered senses."

sanskrit: bhaved dhato 'yaṃ vātāpir agastyeneva mā gatiḥ iha tvaṃ bhava saṃnaddho yantrito rakṣa maithilīm
english: "This one shall be slain as Vātāpi was by Agastya — may his fate be no different. Here you remain armed and disciplined, and guard Maithilī."

sanskrit: asyām āyattam asmākaṃ yat kṛtyaṃ raghunandana aham enaṃ vadhiṣyāmi grahīṣyāmy atha vā mṛgam
english: "O delight of the Raghu line, the task that must be done by us depends on her safety. I shall either kill this one or take the deer alive."

sanskrit: yāvad gacchāmi saumitre mṛgam ānayituṃ drutam paśya lakṣmaṇa vaidehīṃ mṛgatvaci gataspṛhām
english: "Until I go swiftly, O son of Sumitrā, to bring the deer — watch over Vaidehī, O Lakṣmaṇa, whose longing is set upon the deer-hide."

sanskrit: tvacā pradhānayā hy eṣa mṛgo 'dya na bhaviṣyati apramattena te bhāvyam āśramasthena sītayā
english: "For today this deer shall not escape, its hide being the chief prize. You must be vigilant, remaining at the hermitage with Sītā."

sanskrit: yāvat pṛṣatam ekena sāyakena nihanmy aham hatvaitac carma ādāya śīghram eṣyāmi lakṣmaṇa
english: "I shall slay the spotted deer with a single arrow; having slain it and taken its hide, I will return quickly, O Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇenātibalena pakṣiṇā jaṭāyuṣā buddhimatā ca lakṣmaṇa bhavāpramattaḥ pratigṛhya maithilīṃ pratikṣaṇaṃ sarvata eva śaṅkitaḥ
english: "With the auspicious, exceedingly mighty bird Jaṭāyu, wise as he is, present on the right hand, O Lakṣmaṇa, be vigilant — guard Maithilī every moment, alert in every direction."

sanskrit: tathā tu taṃ samādiśya bhrātaraṃ raghunandanaḥ babandhāsiṃ mahātejā jāmbūnadamayatsarum
english: Having instructed his brother thus, the delight of the Raghu line, of great splendor, girded on his sword with a hilt of jāmbūnada gold.

sanskrit: tatas triviṇataṃ cāpam ādāyātmavibhūṣaṇam ābadhya ca kalāpau dvau jagāmodagravikramaḥ
english: Then taking up his triple-bent bow, the ornament of his person, and fastening on two quivers, he set out, striding with bold steps.

sanskrit: taṃ vañcayāno rājendram āpatantaṃ nirīkṣya vai babhūvāntarhitas trāsāt punaḥ saṃdarśane 'bhavat
english: Deceiving him — having looked at the approaching king of kings — the deer vanished from sight out of fear; then it reappeared once more.

sanskrit: baddhāsir dhanur ādāya pradudrāva yato mṛgaḥ taṃ sa paśyati rūpeṇa dyotamānam ivāgrataḥ
english: With sword girded and bow in hand, he ran in the direction of the deer; he beheld it shining before him, as if ablaze with its own radiance.

sanskrit: avekṣyāvekṣya dhāvantaṃ dhanuṣpāṇir mahāvane ativṛttam iṣoḥ pātāl lobhayānaṃ kadā cana
english: Again and again glancing back, the bow-bearing deer fled through the great forest, sometimes advancing beyond arrow's range, then luring him on.

sanskrit: śaṅkitaṃ tu samudbhrāntam utpatantam ivāmbare daśyamānam adṛśyaṃ ca navoddeśeṣu keṣu cit
english: Alarmed and agitated, leaping as if into the sky, now visible and now invisible in certain new spots—

sanskrit: chinnābhrair iva saṃvītaṃ śāradaṃ candramaṇḍalam muhūrtād eva dadṛśe muhur dūrāt prakāśate
english: —like the autumn moon's disk veiled by scattered clouds, it appeared only for a moment, then shone out repeatedly from afar.

sanskrit: darśanādarśanenaiva so 'pākarṣata rāghavam āsīt kruddhas tu kākutstho vivaśas tena mohitaḥ
english: By this repeated appearing and disappearing he drew Rāghava far away; Kākutstha grew angry, yet was helpless, deluded by him.

sanskrit: athāvatasthe suśrāntaś chāyām āśritya śādvale mṛgaiḥ parivṛto vanyair adūrāt pratyadṛśyata
english: Then the deer halted, exhausted, taking refuge in the shade in a green meadow, and was seen from not far away, surrounded by wild deer.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā rāmo mahātejās taṃ hantuṃ kṛtaniścayaḥ saṃdhāya sudṛḍhe cāpe vikṛṣya balavad balī
english: Seeing it, Rāma of great splendor, resolute in his intention to slay it, notched an arrow to his firm bow and drew it back with great force, he of mighty strength—

sanskrit: tam eva mṛgam uddiśya jvalantam iva pannagam mumoca jvalitaṃ dīptam astrabrahmavinirmitam
english: —and aiming at that very deer, let fly a blazing, flaming arrow, bright as a glowing serpent, fashioned by the divine weapons-lore of Brahman.

sanskrit: sa bhṛśaṃ mṛgarūpasya vinirbhidya śarottamaḥ mārīcasyaiva hṛdayaṃ vibhedāśanisaṃnibhaḥ
english: That foremost arrow, piercing violently through the deer-form, cleaved the very heart of Mārīca like a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tālamātram athotpatya nyapatat sa śarāturaḥ vyanadad bhairavaṃ nādaṃ dharaṇyām alpajīvitaḥ mriyamāṇas tu mārīco jahau tāṃ kṛtrimāṃ tanum
english: Leaping up the height of a tāla tree, he fell wounded by the arrow, crying out a dreadful cry as he fell to the earth, his life almost gone; dying, Mārīca abandoned that artificial body.

sanskrit: saṃprāptakālam ājñāya cakāra ca tataḥ svaram sadṛśaṃ rāghavasyaiva hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
english: Knowing the appointed moment had come, he then uttered a voice exactly like Rāghava's own, crying: "Ah, Sītā! Lakṣmaṇa!"

sanskrit: tena marmaṇi nirviddhaḥ śareṇānupamena hi mṛgarūpaṃ tu tat tyaktvā rākṣasaṃ rūpam ātmanaḥ cakre sa sumahākāyo mārīco jīvitaṃ tyajan
english: Pierced to the vital core by that incomparable arrow, abandoning the deer-form, Mārīca, that immense-bodied one, took on his own rākṣasa form as he gave up his life.

sanskrit: tato vicitrakeyūraḥ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ hemamālī mahādaṃṣṭro rākṣaso 'bhūc charāhataḥ
english: Thereupon, struck by the arrow, the rākṣasa appeared with variegated armlets, adorned with all his ornaments, wearing a golden garland, with great fangs.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā patitaṃ bhūmau rākṣasaṃ ghoradarśanam jagāma manasā sītāṃ lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ smaran
english: Seeing that rākṣasa of dreadful appearance fallen to the ground, Rāma went in mind to Sītā, remembering the words of Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: hā sīte lakṣmaṇety evam ākruśya tu mahāsvaram mamāra rākṣasaḥ so 'yaṃ śrutvā sītā kathaṃ bhavet
english: "Having cried out thus, 'Ah, Sītā! Lakṣmaṇa!' with a great voice, this rākṣasa has died — upon hearing that, what will become of Sītā?"

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś ca mahābāhuḥ kām avasthāṃ gamiṣyati iti saṃcintya dharmātmā rāmo hṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ
english: "And to what state will the mighty-armed Lakṣmaṇa be driven?" — reflecting thus, the righteous Rāma felt his body hair bristle with apprehension.

sanskrit: tatra rāmaṃ bhayaṃ tīvram āviveśa viṣādajam rākṣasaṃ mṛgarūpaṃ taṃ hatvā śrutvā ca tat svaram
english: There, having slain that rākṣasa in deer-form and having heard that cry, a sharp fear born of anguish entered Rāma.

sanskrit: nihatya pṛṣataṃ cānyaṃ māṃsam ādāya rāghavaḥ tvaramāṇo janasthānaṃ sasārābhimukhas tadā
english: Having slain another spotted deer and taken its flesh, Rāghava ran in haste, making his way back toward Janasthāna.
